skill.name: dependency-sync
skill.description: Find new imports in modified code, map them to packages, and update dependency manifests with the detected package manager.
skill.summary: Keep dependency manifests synchronized with imports across Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Go, and Flutter projects.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown syntax, built-in module lists, or mapping examples and are false positives. Eight findings are confirmed because the skill directs agents to run package-manager commands with inferred package names. Default automatic installation and commit settings create supply-chain and repository-integrity risks.

remediation.issue: Automatic package installation is enabled without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Default AUTO_INSTALL to false and PROMPT_BEFORE_INSTALL to true. Show each package, version, source registry, target manifest, and command before approval.

remediation.issue: Unknown imports can become registry package names without trust validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require an allowlist or explicit approval for fallback mappings. Pin versions, inspect package metadata, and disable installation scripts when the package manager supports it.

remediation.issue: Repository commits are enabled by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default COMMIT_CHANGES to false. Require review of manifest and lockfile diffs before creating a commit.

content.value_statement: New imports can leave dependency manifests incomplete and break builds. This skill detects missing packages, selects the package manager, and updates the relevant manifest.
actual_capabilities: Detects modified Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and Rust files from git changes or task context.
Parses common import and require patterns from modified source files.
Excludes documented Python standard-library and Node.js built-in modules.
Maps common import aliases and subpaths to installable package names.
Selects uv, Poetry, pip, npm, Yarn, pnpm, Cargo, Go, or Flutter commands from project manifests.
Classifies dependencies as production or development using file locations and package patterns.
limitations: Heuristic mappings can resolve uncommon or ambiguous imports to the wrong registry package.
The skill does not assess package ownership, reputation, vulnerabilities, or malicious installation scripts.
Package installation requires network access and can modify manifests and lockfiles.
Default settings permit installation and repository commits without user approval.

use_cases.title: Complete Application Manifests
use_cases.description: Find packages introduced by recent application changes and add them to the correct production dependency section.

use_cases.title: Register Test Tooling
use_cases.description: Detect test-only imports and place frameworks, linters, and type packages in development dependencies.

use_cases.title: Review Dependency Drift
use_cases.description: Compare changed imports with manifests before release and produce a focused list of missing dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Missing Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review imports in modified files and list missing dependencies. Do not install packages or edit files. Explain each import-to-package mapping.

prompt_templates.title: Synchronize a Python Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Check changed Python files against the active manifest. Ask before installing each missing package, then update the correct production or development group.

prompt_templates.title: Synchronize a Mixed Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect changed Python and TypeScript files. Detect each project manifest, group missing packages by package manager, and request approval before every command.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Guarded Dependency Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit modified imports, reject ambiguous mappings, verify exact registry packages, propose pinned versions, and show manifest changes. Install and commit only after explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Review changed Python files and report missing dependencies without installation.
output: Detected asyncpg in an application module and pytest-asyncio in a test module.
Proposed asyncpg as production and pytest-asyncio as development.
No files or packages were changed.

output_examples.input: Synchronize new TypeScript imports after I approve each package.
output_examples.output: The review proposed zod for production and vitest for development. Both packages remained pending until approval.

output_examples.input: Check a repository where all imports are already declared.
output_examples.output: All detected imports matched existing manifest entries. No dependency changes were required.

best_practices: Require explicit approval for every package name, version, registry, and installation command.
Review manifest and lockfile diffs before running tests or creating a commit.
Run vulnerability checks and project tests after approved dependency changes.
anti_patterns: Do not install a package solely because its registry name matches an import.
Do not select a package manager without confirming the project manifest and lockfile.
Do not commit dependency changes before reviewing package provenance and repository diffs.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It documents import detection for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and Rust.

faq.question: Which package managers are supported?
faq.answer: It covers uv, Poetry, pip, npm, Yarn, pnpm, Bun, Cargo, Go modules, and Flutter pub.

faq.question: Can it distinguish development dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses test file locations and known test, type, lint, and build package patterns.

faq.question: Does it install packages automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, automatic installation is the documented default. Enable confirmation or disable installation before using it on untrusted changes.

faq.question: Does it verify package safety?
faq.answer: No. Registry existence does not establish ownership, reputation, vulnerability status, or safe installation behavior.

faq.question: Can it commit manifest changes?
faq.answer: Yes, commits are enabled by default. Disable this setting until manifest and lockfile changes pass review.
